rules.name: The Only-The-Case-Is-Lit Rule
rules.body: No gradients, no glows, no shadows. Every surface the film draws is a flat fill or a stroke. The only shading in the frame is light on the 3D case (and whatever is in a filmed clip). Lit dots are marks, not glows.

rules.name: The Case-Hangs Rule
rules.body: With no contact shadow the case is not standing on anything, and it is not drawn as if it were. It is placed by where the chapter needs it, and it may cross the horizon.

rules.name: The Case-Travels Rule
rules.body: The case is in the frame whenever the film is drawing. It moves between placements on `glide`; it is never faded, cut to, or cut away from. A move that cannot be shown happens behind a clip.

rules.name: The Complete-Card Rule
rules.body: The first frame and the last frame are complete, legible cards, because they are what a player shows when the film is not playing.

rules.name: The 32 Rule
rules.body: Nothing is set smaller than 32 px. Embedded in a web page the film is shown at under half its size, and 32 is the least that still reads there.

rules.name: The Measured-On-Dots Rule
rules.body: Anything measured (the cursor, the signal, a count) is shown on a dot-matrix display of the one kind, not on a line chart or a bar.

rules.name: The Replayed-Not-Animated Rule
rules.body: Motion presented as real is a recording replayed through the app's engine. Hand-posed motion is used only to explain, and is never captioned as real.

rules.name: The Opaque-Clip Rule
rules.body: A clip's frame opens from a line and closes to one, between the margins, and is opaque throughout. The stage is never seen through it or dissolved into it.

dos: Do take every colour and text style from `Look`, and every time from `At`.
Do start every text block at the 150 px margin and keep the case to the right of it.
Do bring a headline in with `reveal` and everything else that is text with `lift`.
Do move the case with a new placement and a `glide`, starting just before the chapter that needs it.
Do show a new measurement on a dot display with the shared face, the screen's dot spacing, and `key` for what was counted.
Do cut real motion from the recording with `Take.cut`, and say on screen that it is a recording.
Do re-read the first and last frames after any change to the opening or the end.
Do keep each chapter to one headline and at most two sentences.
donts: Don't add a gradient, a glow, a shadow or a blur to anything the film draws, including the dot screen's glow and the contact shadow from the app.
Don't stand the case on the floor or give it a ground to sit on.
Don't fade the case in or out, or cut between two views of it.
Don't set anything smaller than 32 px, or shrink a label to make it fit.
Don't let anything show through the clip frame, or cross-dissolve into a clip.
Don't animate by hand something the film presents as the engine's output: a cursor path, a tap, a verdict.
Don't add a second accent, or use `key` for decoration; it marks what is lit, live or counted.
Don't treat the placeholder card as a component, or describe the clips, the sound or the chapter order as settled until the user has supplied or confirmed them.
notCanonized: The placeholder card and its 'Clip A' line in key above the title: a production note that goes when the clips arrive.

narrative.overview:
The window is a small room. A dot-matrix screen hangs on a pale wall, the AirPods case stands on the floor beneath it, and the dot being aimed is lit on that screen. Everything is a mirror of the hand: the case on screen turns as the real one turns, the lit dot is the real cursor, and a tap answers twice at once, as a ring spreading from behind the case and a ring of dots on the screen. The app's settings are not a sidebar of grouped rows; they are four large pills along the bottom, each opening one white panel beside the stage.

The materials are few. The room is cool matte white by day and deep blue-black at night. One sky-blue keyline outlines what can be acted on and lights what is live. Forms are pebbles: capsules, a 22 pt continuous-corner panel, round dots. The only glossy object is the case, rendered in 3D with physically based white plastic; everything drawn in SwiftUI is flat and matte. Targets are large, because the pointer being configured is often the one doing the clicking, from arm's length.

It is a tool to be opened, tuned and closed. Text says what is happening and the physical thing to do about it, in a rounded display line and one plain line under it.
keyCharacteristics: A stage (screen over case over status line) that is the whole idea in one picture; panels open beside it, never over it.
One accent in two strengths: `keyline` for outlines and lit things, `action` for fills and accent text.
Capsule pills at three heights (30, 38, 48 pt), outlined in the keyline.
A dot-matrix miniature of the real display, 40 by 26 dots, showing the real cursor.
One glossy object, the case, white in both appearances.
Native Mac controls (slider, switch, segmented picker) tinted with `action`, not redrawn.
Motion only as an answer to state: a tap, a lid, a panel, a switch.

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: There is one accent hue. `keyline` draws lines and lit things; `action` fills controls and colours text. A second hue is never added for emphasis, category or decoration.

rules.name: The Only-You-Can-Fix-It Rule
rules.body: `warn` marks a thing only the user can fix (a permission, Automatic Ear Detection). It is never decorative, never a generic "notice", and never used for a state that fixes itself, which is shown in `ink-soft` as waiting.

rules.name: The Outline-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: By day the keyline is too light for text. Anything that must be read in the accent uses `action`.

rules.name: The Changing-Number Rule
rules.body: A number that can change on screen is set in `figure`, so its digits do not shift as it changes.

rules.name: The Panel-Says-What-It-Is-For Rule
rules.body: A panel opens with a plain sentence in `title` ("How the cursor answers your hand"), not a label and not the tab's name again.

rules.name: The Stage-Stays Rule
rules.body: The case and the screen stay in view whatever else is open. Controls go in the panel beside the stage; nothing covers it and nothing replaces it, including first-run setup.

rules.name: The Fit-First Rule
rules.body: A panel is composed to fit its height without scrolling. Where it cannot (Setup), the bottom edge fades to `panel` over 56 pt and a `chevron.compact.down` in `action` says there is more; both disappear at the end of the scroll.

rules.name: The Arm's-Length Rule
rules.body: Anything clicked often is large: tab pills are 48 pt high with a 92 pt minimum label, native sliders and segmented pickers use the large control size, and nothing needs a hover to be understood.

rules.name: The Dark-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never the `ink` token, which turns pale at night. Use `Theme.shadow(strength)`, which is dark in both appearances.

rules.name: The One-Glow Rule
rules.body: The only glow around a surface is the dot screen's: keyline-coloured, and present only while the pointer is live. Lit dots, the case's status light and the tap rings are lit marks, not glows; no other surface gets a coloured halo.

rules.name: The One-Glossy-Object Rule
rules.body: Nothing drawn by the app is glossy except the case. No sheen, glass or specular highlight on pills, panels or the screen. Native controls keep whatever material the system gives them.

dos: Do take every colour from `Theme` and every text style from `Typo`; both appearances come with the token.
Do use `keyline` for outlines and lit things and `action` for fills and accent text.
Do make the next step a primary pill, other actions secondary pills, and the least important one quiet; one primary per group.
Do put new controls in a panel beside the stage, opening with a `title` sentence and separated into groups by a title and a hairline.
Do use native sliders, switches and segmented pickers at the large size, tinted `action`.
Do set every changing number in `figure`.
Do cast shadows with `Theme.shadow(strength)`, soft and straight down.
Do show the case asleep by a shut lid and an unlit status light, and keep it white in both appearances.
Do tie every animation to a change of state, on `quick` or `settle`, with a fade in its place under Reduce Motion.
Do say what is wrong and the physical fix, in the status line or the row's caption.
donts: Don't build a Settings sidebar of grouped rows, or box groups inside the panel.
Don't add a second accent hue, or use `warn` for anything the user cannot fix themselves.
Don't use the `ink` token as a shadow colour.
Don't add a glow to anything but the live dot screen.
Don't make anything glossy except the case: no sheen, glass or highlight on pills, panels or the screen.
Don't dim or tint the case to show a state.
Don't set text in `keyline` by day.
Don't let a panel scroll when it could be made to fit; where it must, keep the fade and the chevron.
Don't add idle or decorative motion, or bounce.
Don't cover the stage or make anything depend on hover to be understood.
